intro: Phoenix landed at 68.22°N on May 25, 2008 — the first NASA lander to touch down in the Martian high arctic. Within days it had scooped up the first sample of Martian water ice and watched it sublimate in the camera frame. The lander operated for 157 sols until the polar winter killed it; CO₂ frost formation buried the solar panels, ending the mission.
